Max Brooks is the founder of NorthCannon. Before starting NorthCannon in 2026, he spent close to a decade in data and analytics engineering — most recently as Director of Business Intelligence for a multi-state legal services enterprise, building governed reporting and data-model infrastructure across data-heavy operating environments. He holds a B.A. in Economics from Binghamton University and is a Certified Scrum Product Owner. NorthCannon is his first company.

AI should be able to reason without asking us to simply trust that it reasoned correctly.

NorthCannon is working toward a future where machine intelligence can operate over persistent, verifiable state rather than repeatedly reconstructing the world from prompts and context alone.

The goal is not to make probabilistic models deterministic. It is to build an assurance layer around them: preserving what is known, where it came from, when it was valid, what changed, why it changed, and what evidence supports a consequential decision.

That also means treating change itself as first-class intelligence. NorthCannon is designed to understand how facts, rules, evidence, dependencies, and environmental conditions evolve over time; determine which prior conclusions are affected; and trigger the right re-evaluation rather than forcing a system to start from scratch.

NorthCannon is beginning with regulated decision systems, where provenance, reproducibility, temporal accuracy, explicit uncertainty, and change awareness are requirements rather than conveniences. The longer-term vision is broader: infrastructure that allows increasingly capable AI systems to remain grounded in evidence as they reason, act, adapt, and evolve.

Trusted machine intelligence should not only know what is true. It should know when truth changes, what that change affects, and how to prove it.

Gate 1 is NorthCannon’s first controlled falsification benchmark. It tests the persistent verified-state thesis on a pre-authored synthetic corpus using comparison arms, evaluation rules, and metrics defined before execution. The design undergoes independent technical review and adversarial stress testing before execution, and results will be published after the run.
